title: Discussion #6192 — why @onready is an annotation, not a keyword

blocks.text:
In Godot 4.0 beta, the onready keyword became the @onready annotation.
The GDScript docs said annotations "affect how the script is treated by
external tools and usually don't change the behavior." @onready appears to
violate both: it is internal to the node (not an external-tool concern)
and it does change when the assignment runs (_ready vs construction).
The proposal was to restore onready as a keyword, both for consistency
with that distinction and because many @ signs add visual noise.

Maintainer response: this is more of a bug in the documentation than a
reason to revert the syntax. @export annotations affect get_property_list()
and duplicate() (exported variables are copied; others are not). The @rpc
annotation has a very large effect on behavior too. The GDScript team
discussed annotations vs keywords and reached a consensus that existing
keywords and annotations should not be changed, even without a general
rule for new features. The confusing "usually don't change the behavior"
sentence was corrected in the user manual (godot-docs#9188).
